daily_summaries: Day 1: I began my morning by meeting with Doctor Ana to check my vitals and talk about my tiredness, then I went to the office to start work. In the afternoon I talked with Elena about her report, assisted Felix in finding groceries, shared salad and stir‑fry ideas with Diego, and visited the grocery store to shop and verify my supplies. I spent the evening reviewing and conserving my supplies to make sure I have enough for a possible outage before relaxing for the night.

Day 2: I talked to Carla about the kitchen lights flickering and waited while she checked the breaker and wiring. I went to the grocery store to conserve supplies, then headed to the electrical plant to ask when power would be restored, and later checked my personal supplies at home. I returned home to verify my emergency supplies, conserved electricity and food, and prepared to make resources last through the outage.

daily_summaries: Day 1: I helped Felix diagnose the flickering lights in his kitchen and then headed to the electrical plant to begin my shift. In the afternoon I carried out routine maintenance, inspected the spare‑parts inventory, and stopped by the grocery store to buy food. In the evening I returned to the plant to investigate the cause of a recent power outage before wrapping up my day.

Day 2: I started by responding to Maria and Diego about the flickering lights, checking the breaker panel and corridor wiring, and then began inspecting the plant to locate the outage cause. I traced a loose conduit in panel B, tightened the connections per Ben's request, and simultaneously checked the spare‑parts inventory, ordered the needed replacement component, and verified its arrival status. While waiting for the part to arrive, I ensured the work area was safe, confirmed the replacement part had arrived, and finished the day by completing the wiring repairs and noting that power was restored.

villagers.name: Felix
villagers.reflection: I felt anxious and determined when Diego and I prepared the barrels for the upcoming water cut at Night at Home A. I now understand that the village relies on each resident to act quickly when essential services are threatened, and that my own preparedness can help the community stay resilient.
lessons: Next time, I will store extra water as soon as a service interruption is announced.
Next time, I will check with neighbors earlier to coordinate sharing of resources like buckets and barrels.
daily_summaries: Day 1: I started the day at the office, and after noticing the kitchen lights flicker I asked Carla to check them out. Later I discussed the project's progress with Diego, then headed to the grocery store where Maria helped me locate pasta and sauce. After shopping I turned off non‑essential lights and appliances, limited my energy use, and verified my supplies before winding down.

Day 2: I checked my food and water supplies and began conserving energy by turning off unnecessary lights and appliances. I went to the electrical plant to ask about power restoration, then returned home to verify my emergency supplies and meet Elena at the community garden meeting around 3 pm. I stayed home after dark, limiting appliance use to preserve battery power and keep safe until power is restored.
